subject: Bounded immutable borrowing in the maintained package-lock content reader
claim: The previous inline borrowed matches exceeded the specified WVIR proof limit: the scanner had 281 blocks and 87 parameter/local slots, versus limits of 64 each. Extracting repeated digest-and-size validation into Readˉcontent leaves its single borrowed match within seven blocks, six slots, 28 operations and 25 temporaries. The existing lock tests and 42 added cases pass on Windows and Debian. Normal Project 4 build and native replacement produce identical WVB bytes. No compiler limit, public API or package wire format changed.

limitations: The 42 new cases cover six record positions (origin, package, compiler, project, part, output), each with zero, maximum u64, overflow, leading zero, negative and non-digit input, and simultaneous invalid digest/decimal. Rejections check the exact line and column; digest rejection precedes decimal rejection. Existing valid-lock, ordering, missing-record and duplicate-path cases also run.

The compiler proof bounds are unchanged. The large scanner still has 265 blocks and 79 slots but no payload-borrow operation; the small reader owns the borrow. No general large-function borrowing or improved compiler diagnostic is claimed.
Debian executes a Windows-constructed Linux image. This is not independent Linux construction or complete dual-host qualification.

Only the affected maintained lock fixture was rebuilt and executed in the final run. The unchanged canonical-parser test and lowerer owner retain their prior exact-input evidence; unrelated package, installation and bundle suites were not rerun.

The automatic changed-file plan included pending migration work with expected duration 660 seconds and maximum 2400 seconds. It was inspected but not executed; focused diagnosis and final checks stayed below the ten-minute development budget.

Current lowerer selection remains explicit. The normal package-format owner still needs integration, and shared SHA-256 source-edition reconciliation remains pending. The package migration is not committed; pinned packaging and installed identities are unchanged.
No full transaction fault injection, concurrency suite, installed promotion, peak-memory measurement or independent human review was performed.
